params.stop_fill: worst print: a stop fills at the bar's adverse extreme (a long's LOW), not at the stop; realized_r_house / *_house re-price the same exits at the stop, or at the open when the bar gapped through it

results.conviction_rule: 1W reclaim/break, 3D reclaim or 1D break - armed, grade A/A+

caveats: Survivorship bias — today's universe excludes delisted names.

Data: stocks are yfinance daily bars (dividend-adjusted, occasional gaps); crypto from exchange daily klines (data.fetch) with the live identity check against CoinGecko's price -- a coin no source confirms is left out, Yahoo only for coins no exchange lists. coverage[market].data_sources names the venues.
Intrabar fills assume the stop fills before the target within a bar.

Stop fill: worst print: a stop fills at the bar's adverse extreme (a long's LOW), not at the stop; realized_r_house / *_house re-price the same exits at the stop, or at the open when the bar gapped through it. The headline (realized_r, expectancy_r, total_r) is the worst print; *_house is the owner's house rule (rmodel.HOUSE_STOP_FILL). Exit timing is identical under both, so the two columns describe one set of trades.

Re-entry cooldown: after a full stop-out no new entry on the symbol for params.reentry_cooldown_days (the live bot's rule), applied in the replay itself; coverage[market].cooldown_blocked counts the refused re-entries.
A+ setups are rare, so trade counts (N) can be small and noisy.
4H is not backtested (no deep intraday history).

Dollar columns (total_usd, max_dd_usd) are priced under params.sizing_mode and are NOT comparable across runs that changed it — a switch between risk-% and fixed-notional moves them by an order of magnitude on identical trades. Read total_r and expectancy_r, which are ratios and carry across.

Portfolio sim: the weekly/3d LEVEL gate, the slot/symbol/sector/cooldown caps and the price + stop-distance gates ARE replayed; the time stop, the daily/weekly loss guards, the earnings buffer and the ADV gates are not (no intra-trade price paths, earnings calendar or historical volume in the slim records), and it runs one market at a time so cross-market slot contention is not modelled.
